result.topic_en: Euler derives approximate expressions for the uniform-state height v and the quantity R in the theory of fluid friction (efflux through pipes), and discusses the conditions under which efflux becomes uniform.
result.transcription:
366 TENTAMEN THEORIAE

74. Cum igitur ſit poſito $\mathfrak{B}$ valde paruo, ideoque $B=\frac{1}{\alpha}$
$$v=\frac{a\mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{C}+\frac{g}{\alpha}\mathfrak{C}+Cb-l}{1-\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{g}-\alpha C\mathfrak{h}}=\frac{\frac{g}{\alpha}\mathfrak{C}+Cb-l}{1-\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{g}}$$
neglectis terminis minimis, erit
$$\mathfrak{R}=\frac{l-Cb}{\mathfrak{C}}+\frac{(1-\mathfrak{h})\frac{g}{\alpha}}{1-\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{g}}-\frac{(1-\mathfrak{h})(l-Cb)}{\mathfrak{C}(1-\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{g})},\text{ ſiue}$$
$$\mathfrak{R}=\frac{(1-\mathfrak{h})\frac{g}{\alpha}}{1-\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{g}}-\frac{(\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{g}-\mathfrak{h})(l-Cb)}{\mathfrak{C}(1-\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{g})}$$
At cum ſit proxime $\mathfrak{C}=1$ et $Cb=c$, erit
$$v=\frac{\frac{g}{\alpha}+c-l}{1-\mathfrak{g}}\text{ et }\mathfrak{R}=\frac{\frac{g}{\alpha}(1-\mathfrak{h})-(\mathfrak{g}-\mathfrak{h})(l-c)}{1-\mathfrak{g}}$$

75. Hinc primo patet, ſi fuerit $\mathfrak{g}=1$ vel $\mathfrak{g}>1$, effluxum nunquam ad ſtatum vniformitatis reduci, ideoque motum ex his formulis, quae ad hunc ſtatum ſunt accommodatae, definiri omnino non poſſe; ſtatim ergo ab initio calculus ita adornari debuiſſet, vt altitudo $v$, tanquam variabilis, eſſet introducta. Quodſi autem fuerit $\mathfrak{g}<1$, ſeu $kk<gg$, effluxus quidem vniformis euadet, et aqua effluet, ſi fuerit $\frac{g}{\alpha}+c>l$, ſimulque $\frac{g}{\alpha}(1-\mathfrak{h})>(\mathfrak{g}-\mathfrak{h})(l-c)$; ſin autem ſit $\frac{g}{\alpha}+c=l$, ſeu $\frac{g}{\alpha}+c<l$, aqua plane non effluet, exiſtente, vti aſſumimus, $kk<gg$. At ſi ſit $\frac{g}{\alpha}+c>l$, puta $\frac{g}{\alpha}+c=l+\gamma$, effluxus ad vniformitatem perueniet, quoties fuerit $c<l$. Caſibus autem, quibus $c>l$, hoc multo magis eueniet, quia, ob $\mathfrak{h}<\mathfrak{g}$, tum valor ipſius $\mathfrak{R}$ ſemper eſt affirmatiuus.

CASVS

items.quote: Hinc primo patet, ſi fuerit $\mathfrak{g}=1$ vel $\mathfrak{g}>1$, effluxum nunquam ad ſtatum vniformitatis reduci
items.english: Hence it is first evident that if g = 1 or g > 1, the efflux is never reduced to a uniform state.

items.quote: Quodſi autem fuerit $\mathfrak{g}<1$, ſeu $kk<gg$, effluxus quidem vniformis euadet, et aqua effluet, ſi fuerit $\frac{g}{\alpha}+c>l$, ſimulque $\frac{g}{\alpha}(1-\mathfrak{h})>(\mathfrak{g}-\mathfrak{h})(l-c)$
items.english: But if g < 1, i.e. kk < gg, the efflux will become uniform, and water will flow out if g/α + c > l and at the same time g/α(1−h) > (g−h)(l−c).

items.quote: At ſi ſit $\frac{g}{\alpha}+c>l$, puta $\frac{g}{\alpha}+c=l+\gamma$, effluxus ad vniformitatem perueniet, quoties fuerit $c<l$.
items.english: But if g/α + c > l, say g/α + c = l + γ, the efflux will reach uniformity whenever c < l.
